The Guardian issued a series of corrections to its recent articles, clarifying several factual errors that had appeared in print.

* Additional amendments noted that Eileen Burbidge is the executive director of Fertifa, not its founder; Juliet Stevenson referred to director Alex Lawther, not “Lowther”; the family in Bend It Like Beckham is Sikh, not Muslim; and it was Venetia Stanley’s uncle, the third Baron Stanley, who converted to Islam, not her father.

***

Other revisions included updates on the Telegram founder’s arrest at a French airport, features on royal servants in new exhibitions, commentary on the Pope’s view of England’s football tactics, analysis of Britain’s potential as a sci‑tech hub, coverage of the Salvator Mundi controversy, and a note about the last of the summer wines.

Section 4
Readers wishing to comment can write to the Readers’ Editor at the Observer, York Way, London N1 9GU, email observer.readers@observer.co.uk, or call 020 3353 4736.
P.P.S Remember to double‑check details before publishing to avoid similar corrections.
